title: Developmental Psychology Adventure 1: Piaget's Cognitive Stages
welcome_lead: Today you'll climb Piaget's four stages of cognitive development.
meta_desc: Psychology Developmental: Piaget's four stages — sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational, formal.
final_note: You sequenced Piaget's four cognitive stages and key milestones.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Jean Piaget (1936) saw children as 'little scientists' building schemas.

Sensorimotor (0–2): learn through senses and motion; gain object permanence (~8 mo).

Preoperational (2–7): language, symbolic play, but egocentric (three mountains task, Piaget & Inhelder, 1956) and lacks conservation.

Concrete operational (7–11): can conserve number, mass, volume; reversibility, classification — but only for concrete cases.

Formal operational (11+): abstract and hypothetical reasoning; the pendulum task tests systematic hypothesis testing.

Strengths: revolutionised child research, drove discovery learning in education.

Limits: Hughes (1975) 'naughty teddy' task showed children younger than 4 can conserve; Gelman (1979) showed early numerical competence; cultural bias (Dasen 1994) — Aboriginal children gain spatial concepts before number.
